ny_mckenzie_pond_boulders.blurb: This boulder cluster sits along McKenzie Pond Road in the Adirondacks, close to Saranac Lake and Lake Placid. The problems are split across four sets, numbered First through Fourth, with the First Set holding the most climbs and the Second Set close behind. Many of the boulders are house-sized glacial leftovers, and the problems tend to be tall, with mostly safe landings and a few that call for extra pads. It is all bouldering. Grades start at V0 and reach a handful of V9s, but the bulk of the problems sit between V0 and V4, so there is plenty for newer boulderers alongside some hard lines for strong ones.

sd_blue_sky.blurb: Blue Sky is a group of walls in Spearfish Canyon, South Dakota. The canyon itself is limestone, and Blue Sky is among the parts of it known for especially good stone. The climbing is technical, on mostly vertical to slightly overhanging walls with small pockets and edges. Sport routes make up the bulk of it, with a smaller number of boulder problems, including a set of roadside boulders. Most routes fall between 5.11 and 5.12, with a good number of 5.10s and a few 5.13s. Indecent Exposure holds the most climbs, followed by Iron Horse Wall and Pheromone Wall. Lord of the Flies Wall is the first wall reached, and mixes some warm-ups with several 5.12s.

tx_franklin_mountain_range.blurb: The Franklin Mountains rise on the northern edge of El Paso in far west Texas, a desert range in Chihuahuan Desert surroundings. The climbing is varied: sport routes, trad lines and boulder problems in similar numbers, plus a few top-rope climbs, across a wide spread of grades from easy to the 5.12 range. McKelligon Canyon is on the east side of El Paso, and Tom Mays Park is on the west side. Crazy Cat, also called the Palisades, is mostly bouldering. Smaller crags include Mammoth Rock, Anthony's Bluff and Lost Padre Wall.

wa_larrabee.blurb: Larrabee is in Larrabee State Park, about six miles south of Bellingham, Washington, where some of the walls sit beside the ocean and the railway. Bouldering dominates, and most of it is at Lost Ledge, which holds the most climbs, followed by Clayton Beach. At Lost Ledge the rock is Chuckanut sandstone, with many problems set among trees. The roped climbing is a small share: a handful of top-rope, sport and trad routes at spots such as Desperation, The Gray Wall and Boat Launch Wall. Boulder problems run from V0 up to about V9, mostly V0 to V5, while the roped routes mostly fall between 5.7 and 5.10.

az_kelly_canyon.blurb: Kelly Canyon is a bouldering area a few miles south of Flagstaff in northern Arizona, at about 7,000 feet in a peaceful forested canyon. The rock is Coconino sandstone, and it varies from hard and grippy in places to sandy in others. The walls have curving features that make for slopey, technical climbing, and many problems are highballs with committing, sloping top-outs. The sandstone is fragile when wet. Grades are spread fairly evenly from V0 to V6, with a smaller number from V7 to V9. East Kelly Canyon holds the most climbs, with West Kelly Canyon smaller. Fall is the prime season; summer can be hot, though shade is easy to find.
